title: Equivalent Fractions: Fuel Tank Fix
subtitle: Fractions · Mission 02
tagline: Calibrate the fuel tank by finding {{cyan:equivalent fractions}} — same fuel, different slices.

slides.headline: The ship's fuel tank is out of calibration.
body: Engineering needs the tank filled to match a target fraction — but the tank you have is sliced differently than the target. Same fuel, different slices.
Your job: pick a **multiplier** that re-slices your tank so its fill can equal the target. Then fill it. When your fill is `equivalent` to the target, the ship starts.
Three calibrations. Each one asks for a different target. Continue unlocks when your fuel is equivalent.

prompt.label: LEVEL 1 · HALVES
prompt.question: Target: `1 / 2`. Slice your tank and fill it until your fuel is equivalent to one-half.

correct.title: ✓ TANK CALIBRATED
body: You matched `1 / 2`. Any equivalent works — `2/4`, `3/6`, `4/8`, `5/10` — because multiplying the numerator and denominator by the same number doesn't change the fraction's value.
That's what `equivalent fractions` means: different names, same amount.
correct.followup: The multiplier you picked cut each part of the tank into equal sub-parts. If you doubled the denominator, you had to double the numerator to keep the fill the same.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ KEEP CALIBRATING
body: Not equivalent yet. Watch the equation preview — the fraction after the `=` sign is what your tank needs to read.

config.instruction: Pick a multiplier (1x–4x), then click slices on Your Tank to fill fuel equivalent to 1/2.
config.hint: If you pick 2x, your tank has 4 slices (2 × 2). Half of 4 is 2, so fill 2 slices. If you pick 4x, your tank has 8 slices — fill 4 of them.

prompt.label: LEVEL 2 · TWO-THIRDS
prompt.question: Target: `2 / 3`. Same idea — slice the tank, fill until it matches two-thirds.

correct.title: ✓ TWO-THIRDS LOCKED
body: You produced an equivalent to `2/3`. If you chose 3x, that's `6/9`. If you chose 4x, that's `8/12`. Both name the same amount of fuel.
The `numerator` (top) grew, the `denominator` (bottom) grew — but the *ratio* between them stayed at 2 to 3.
correct.followup: This is the same rule you'll use later for adding fractions with unlike denominators: find a common bottom by re-slicing.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ NOT EQUIVALENT YET
body: Check the equation preview above the tank. The target is `2/3` — your fill needs to match the fraction after the equals sign.

config.instruction: Pick any multiplier, then fill Your Tank until it's equivalent to 2/3.
config.hint: Try 4x. That gives you 12 slices (3 × 4). Two-thirds of 12 is 8 — so fill 8 slices.

prompt.label: LEVEL 3 · CUT INTO FIFTEENTHS
prompt.question: Target: `3 / 5`. Engineering needs the tank cut into **fifteenths** specifically. Pick the right multiplier, then fill.

correct.title: ✓ FIFTEENTHS CERTIFIED
body: **9 out of 15 slices.** `3/5 = 9/15` because 5 × 3 = 15 (the multiplier you picked) and 3 × 3 = 9 (same multiplier, applied to the numerator).
This is the whole move: **multiply top and bottom by the same number** to get an equivalent fraction with a specific denominator.
correct.followup: Later, when you need to add `3/5 + 1/3`, you'll re-slice both fractions to fifteenths first — for the same reason engineering asked for fifteenths here.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ CHECK THE SLICES
body: Two things to check: (1) the multiplier — 5 × ? = 15? — and (2) the fill count, once your tank is sliced right.

config.instruction: Slice the tank into fifteenths (so you need the multiplier that turns 5 into 15), then fill it equivalent to 3/5.
config.hint: 5 × 3 = 15, so pick 3x. That cuts your tank into 15 slices. Three-fifths of 15 is 9 — fill 9 slices.

slides.headline: TANK CALIBRATED
slides.subtext: You calibrated three tanks by finding equivalent fractions. Same fuel, different slice counts — that's the whole move.
